subject: Latency & burst capacity — next steps to validate Hosted vs Dedicated fit
body:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Kai Morgan <kai.morgan@speedlane.com>, Devon Hart <devon.hart@speedlane.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Sep 2028 16:03:00 -0000
Subject: Latency & burst capacity — next steps to validate Hosted vs Dedicated fit

Hi Kai / Devon —

Thanks again for the call today — good conversation and helpful context on the checkout flow and sale-day bursts. Quick recap + asks so we can size a concrete pilot: 

Summary of your constraints (from today's call)
- Core checkout: steady-state ~600 qps (inference requests/sec) with p95 SLA target <= 100 ms
- Peak bursts during promotions: up to ~1.8k qps for short windows (~3-8 minutes)
- Payloads are small (avg 220 tokens) but you have heavy tokenization nuances causing higher compute per request
- Data residency: US-only for now, potential EU expansion next year

Our high-level guidance (to calibrate expectations)
- Hosted API: fast to onboard; ideal for pilots and workloads where sustained qps is <= ~800 and p95 targets are <=200ms. Autoscaling handles bursts but very short intense spikes can experience transient queuing unless we provision burst capacity.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools tuned for stable p95 <120ms at sustained qps in the 1k+ band; provides predictable latency and isolation for QoS-sensitive use cases.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): recommended if you need on-prem data controls or custom networking — not required for SpeedLane at this stage.

Concrete asks / next steps
1) Can you share a short QPS histogram (1-min granularity) from the last 30 days and a sample of typical request payloads? This will help us reproduce the compute characteristics. (Attachment placeholder OK)
2) Indicate how long your promotion bursts last on average (minutes) and any SLA wiggle room for p95 during bursts.
3) Would you prefer we propose: (A) a Hosted pilot with configured burst buffer + alerts, or (B) a Dedicated baseline with Hosted fallback for overflow? We can price both.

If you can send the QPS histogram and a sample payload by EOD Monday, Marissa and I will put together a pilot proposal and expected latency/throughput targets.

Cheers,
Jordan Blake
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
[jordan_blake@redwood.com] | +1 (415) 555-0182

From: Kai Morgan <kai.morgan@speedlane.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Devon Hart <devon.hart@speedlane.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Sep 2028 10:22:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Latency & burst capacity — next steps to validate Hosted vs Dedicated fit

Thanks Jordan —

Good recap. Attaching the QPS export (last 30 days) — see speedlane_qps_report.csv. A couple clarifications: 
- Bursts usually come in 3–6 minute waves, sometimes a series over an hour during heavy promotions.
- Our absolute requirement is p95 <= 120 ms for checkout-critical requests; sub-100ms would be ideal.
- We have a hard cap on failed/slow checkouts — anything above 250 ms causes checkout abandonment that we want to avoid.

We'd like option B (Dedicated baseline with Hosted overflow) if Dedicated can guarantee p95 <= 120 ms at steady 600 qps and sustain spikes to 1.8k with graceful degradation. Please include any short-term reserved capacity pricing and what the typical lead time is to spin dedicated pool.

—Kai
Kai Morgan
Head of Platform Engineering, SpeedLane
kai.morgan@speedlane.com | 415-800-3321

Attachment: speedlane_qps_report.csv (CSV, 92KB)

On: Sat, 15 Sep 2028 12:47:00 -0000 Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com> wrote:
> Lauren / Marissa — looping you in. Kai just sent the QPS export and confirmed they prefer Dedicated baseline + Hosted overflow. Their p95 target is <=120ms at steady 600 qps, bursts to 1.8k for ~3–6 minutes.
>
> Thoughts on:
> - viability of a Dedicated pilot sized for 600 qps steady with a 2.5x burst buffer (1.5k) versus needing a 3x buffer to hit 1.8k?
> - pricing outline and any promotional pilot discount we can offer?
> - lead time to spin a dedicated pool (any way to fast-track)?
>
> I think we should propose a 90-day pilot: dedicated baseline for steady-state with Hosted overflow and a 1-week stress window where SpeedLane can run simulated bursts. If ok, I'll draft the mutual action plan and send to Kai.

> Thanks — Jordan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Sep 2028 09:22:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Latency & burst capacity — next steps to validate Hosted vs Dedicated fit

Jordan —

Short answer: go Dedicated baseline + Hosted overflow. Details: 
- Recommendation: size Dedicated for steady 600 qps with headroom for 1k sustained (to cover average elevated load) and rely on Hosted overflow to cover the 1.8k short spikes. This reduces committed cost while giving them predictable tail latency on core traffic.
- Burst buffer math: a 2.5x buffer (1.5k) on Dedicated buys them consistent p95 sub-120ms for most spikes; the remaining spike headroom can be absorbed by Hosted overflow with configured routing policy to prefer Dedicated first, then failover to Hosted if queueing increases.
- Lead time: standard spin-up for Dedicated pool is ~7 business days; we can offer a fast-track 3 business day option for pilots if we mark it as a Priority Proof-of-Concept (requires ops sign-off).
- Pricing: see attached redwood_dedicated_pricing_v2.pdf — propose a pilot discount (20% off list for first 90 days) and an optional commitment credit if they convert to a 6–12 month reserved contract.

Next steps I will take:
1) Draft the mutual action plan and pilot SLOs (latency targets, test windows).
2) Schedule an architect call with our infra team and SpeedLane's platform engineers (Kai / Devon) — propose Wed 9/20 or Thu 9/21.
3) Prepare a fast-track ops request in parallel so we can hit a 3-day pilot if SpeedLane signs LOI.

Happy to review the MAP before we send to Kai.

—Marissa
